 Ahead of Tuesday's election, Fox47.com has you covered with the latest election news.
 Make sure to tune in to the News at 9 on Nov. 3 for News 3 Now's coverage of the election as the polls close. Coverage continues with News 3 Now at Ten.
 Who's on your ballot? 
 Depending on where you live, your ballot may vary compared to others. To find out the candidates, visit the MyVote Wisconsin website . You can enter your address to generate a sample ballot and find your polling place.
 Regardless of where you live, the top race is the one for governor, in which Democrat David Crowley and Republican Tom Tiffany will face each other to replace the retiring Gov. Tony Evers.
 Other notable races include contests for U.S. House of Representatives, Secretary of State, and Attorney General.
 Voter Resources 
 Where do I vote? 
 At this point, in-person absentee voting is closed. If you haven't mailed in your absentee ballot, it's too late to put it in the mailbox and you should instead return it to your local clerk's office.
 That means it's time to make a plan to vote in person. You can find your assigned polling place using the MyVote Wisconsin website.
 In Wisconsin, polls open at 7 a.m. and close at 8 p.m. If you're in line at 8 p.m., stay in line and you'll be allowed to cast your vote.
 What ID do I need to show at polls? 
 Voters who do not have a Wisconsin driver’s license, state ID or another acceptable form of photo identification can get a free Wisconsin state ID card from the Department of Motor Vehicles.
 Wisconsin does not issue a separate voter ID card, and a federally compliant REAL ID is not required to vote.
 According to the Wisconsin Department of Transportation, documentation requirements—such as a birth certificate, proof of identity, and Wisconsin residency—should be presented at the DMV to obtain an official Wisconsin ID card.
